newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANSA GETS EBRD SUBORDINATED LOAN.
newsitem.headline: HANSA GETS EBRD SUBORDINATED LOAN.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development said it has signed a 15 million mark subordinated loan with Estonia's largest bank Hansapank.
The EBRD said in a statement released late on Wednesday that loan has a 10-year term and is to provide long-term loans.

"Designed to increase Hansapank's capital base, the EBRD's loan will support the bank's expansion, particularly its lending activities to the private corporate sector in Estonia," Kurt Geiger, co-director of the EBRD's Financial Institutions team, said in a statement.
The EBRD said that five-year senior debt was now available to Estonian banks on the international market but the EBRD was still the only institution that would extend longer-term subordinated debt.

"The loan replaces an existing 12 million mark credit line which carried a six-year term and for which Hansapank was able to source from the international market at a competitive rate," the statement said.
